clue.text: Dog whistle in part of American's car?

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely, to tail them
a pipe is a simple whistle-like instrument

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dog whistle is some component of a car in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like a noun but it is the verb meaning to follow. The question mark marks the definition as American usage: in the US the exhaust pipe goes by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the exhaust pipe at the back of a vehicle carries this name, so it is a component of a US car.

clue.text: Top end of market gives support to this new couturier, ultimately

indicators.note: gives support to joins the end of market to the rest, the T standing as a base piece of the build
end of means the last letter of market is used
new means remade, so the letters of this, with the couturier's last letter, are rearranged
ultimately means finally, so the last letter of couturier is taken

explanation.surface: The upmarket end of fashion supports a new designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives support to' is link padding; 'Top' is the definition, a garment, not the top of the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sleeved casual garment for the upper body is a top in clothing terms.

clue.text: Out all night? I'd like to be!

definitions.text: Out all night? I'd like to be!

parts.words: Out all night? I'd like to be!
parts.note: being out can mean unconscious, asleep; a sufferer awake all night would love to be out cold

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they are out partying all night replies they wish they were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' suggests a night on the town, but here it means asleep, which this person cannot manage.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who cannot sleep lies awake all night wishing to be out cold.

clue.text: Dull, expert on ketch

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is an expert
a saic is a ketch-like sailing vessel of the eastern Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Someone finds a sailing expert's talk about boats tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: SAIC is an obscure word for a two-masted vessel used in the Levant.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing or life that is commonplace and lacking imagination is described as dull or matter-of-fact.

clue.text: Self-confidence of model entertaining one

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding inside, so the model word goes around the letter for one

parts.note: to pose is to model, as for an artist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fashion model shows composure while hosting a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure and graceful assurance of manner amount to self-possession or confidence.

clue.text: Legendary character international tenor starved of love

indicators.note: starved of means deprived of, so the named letter is taken away from the tenor's name

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was the famous Italian operatic tenor
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A famous international singer is said to be going hungry for affection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek myth tells of the boy who flew too near the sun on wax wings, a figure of legend.

clue.text: Hold check, primarily on nurse

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the first letter of check is taken

parts.note: to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a check on a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' is the definition in the sense of maintain an opinion, not grip.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend that something is true is to assert or maintain it, as one holds a view.

clue.text: Topical variety show? Critical appraisal heard

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the word for critical appraisal is replaced by one that is pronounced the same

parts.note: a review is a critical appraisal

explanation.surface: A satirical stage show gets a critic's assessment that is overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: This theatrical entertainment strings together sketches, songs and dances, often satirising current events.

clue.text: Royalist travelling alone

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters of royalist are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A supporter of the crown makes a journey by themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's own, without companions, is to be by oneself or alone.

clue.text: Willing to appear in quiz programme on TV, for example

definitions.text: quiz programme on TV, for example

parts.note: being game means being willing to try
to show up is to appear, so show can mean appear

explanation.surface: A volunteer is keen to be a contestant on a television quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: A television contest where people answer questions or play for prizes is a quiz programme, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Colonials thrive, unexpectedly, in 'The Scarlet Letter', say

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out in a surprising arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Settlers in a colony flourish against expectation, as in Hawthorne's novel of Puritan New England.
explanation.walkthrough: COLONIALS THRIVE has exactly the fifteen letters needed; the surface nods to the colonial Massachusetts setting of Hawthorne's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorne's 1850 book is set in seventeenth-century Puritan Boston, making it an example of fiction set in the past; 'say' signals an example.

clue.text: Anger about a politician causing storm

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the word for anger is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: anger is rage
MP, Member of Parliament, is the usual crossword politician

explanation.surface: Fury over some politician sets off a storm of protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to rush about violently and destructively, a verb synonym of going on a violent spree.

clue.text: Most serious heading off for tallest peak

indicators.note: heading off means the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: most serious is severest

explanation.surface: The gravest problem facing the expedition is the climb to the world's highest summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan mountain on the Nepal-Tibet border is the highest on Earth, at about 8,849 metres.

clue.text: One initially unwilling to ring the Italian about waterproof material

indicators.note: to ring means to encircle, so the first pieces close around the Italian article and the abbreviation
initially means only the first letter of the word one is used

parts.note: loth (or loath) means reluctant, unwilling
il is the Italian word for the
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone at first reluctant to telephone an Italian about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ring' looks like phoning, but it means encircling: O and LOTH together surround IL and C, giving O + ILC + LOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: This is cotton fabric treated with oil to make it water-resistant, once used for tablecloths and coats.

clue.text: Stubborn old boy expected to cross grass

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: to cross here means to go across, so the word for expected stretches over the grass word

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due
to grass is British slang for informing, and an informer is a rat

explanation.surface: A grumpy old man insists on walking across the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like lawn but is the British slang for an informer, giving RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refuses to change their mind is obstinate and unyielding, hence stubborn.

clue.text: Extremely deceptive, my colour scheme

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outside letters of the word are taken

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a colour scheme that is extremely misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is an exclamation, not a possessive: COR is a British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Interior decoration, the furnishing and colours of a room, is described by this borrowing from French.

clue.text: Eccentric personality's reputation

definitions.meaning: an odd, colourful person is called a real one
a reference describing someone's standing and moral qualities

explanation.surface: A quirky person's standing in the community.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an odd individual and the moral standing or reputation a person has.

clue.text: Close deal over late drink

parts.note: nigh means near, close

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the deal word is read backwards

parts.note: a pact is a deal or agreement

explanation.surface: Two people wrap up a business agreement over a drink late in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink taken just before bed is a drink at the end of the night.

clue.text: Suffer at home: endless wind

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to wind is to curl, as hair winds round a finger

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at home suffers a gale that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as the breeze but is the verb to coil.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring on oneself something unwelcome such as a loss or a penalty is to suffer it.

clue.text: Income from flat in Parisian street

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the flat word goes into the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means level, flat

explanation.surface: Rental earnings from an apartment in a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' reads as an apartment but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: The money an organisation or state takes in is its income, a synonym.

clue.text: Make little of miserable drama

parts.note: feeling down means feeling miserable
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a depressing piece of theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To minimise or treat something as less important than it is means to make little of it.

clue.text: Loyalist, quiet at unruly gathering

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical instruction to play quietly
a riot is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A staunch supporter keeps calm in the middle of a disorderly crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to and vigorously supporting their country is a loyalist to it.

clue.text: Stout, last of beer, locked in room

indicators.note: locked in means shut inside, so that letter goes into the room word

parts.note: a study is a room for working

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of beer

explanation.surface: A dark beer, its last drop shut away in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer, which suits 'beer' in the surface, but is the adjective meaning robust.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongly built and solid, stout and robust are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Worker briefly left royal house

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
left over means remaining, so over can mean left

explanation.surface: An employee left a royal residence after a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb of departure but means remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: The German dynasty supplied British monarchs from George I in 1714 to Victoria.

clue.text: Impressive old gold coin

definitions.meaning: grand, stately and imposing, as in a fine building
an English gold coin first struck under Edward III, worth a third of a pound

explanation.surface: An imposing antique gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means grand or splendid, and the noun was a medieval English gold coin.

clue.text: Passage from another court

parts.note: an extra is one more, another

explanation.surface: An excerpt taken from proceedings in a different court.
explanation.definitionFit: A short section quoted from a book or text is a passage, so the two are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: In Manchester, I called Heather

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone in Manchester telephoned a person called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, low shrubs of moorland.

clue.text: Console member of the clergy and senior politician

parts.note: a console is a cabinet housing a radio, television or controls
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: Comforting a churchman and a prominent politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' looks like the verb to comfort, but it is the noun for a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister sitting in the Cabinet is one of the most senior politicians in Britain.

clue.text: Favour parking by river, free for a change

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: for a change means altered, so the letters of free are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver would rather park by the river at no charge for once.
explanation.definitionFit: To like one option better than another is to favour it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Visual artist capturing head of turbot, a large fish

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the artist's name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Man Ray was the American surrealist photographer and painter

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of turbot

explanation.surface: A painter catches the head of a turbot, which is a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This ray of warm seas is the largest of its kind, with a wingspan up to seven metres.
